descriptionChirho: The proper name Satan, referring to the spiritual adversary and accuser. All three clusters represent the same referent in different grammatical cases (vocative, nominative, genitive, dative, accusative). Multilingual evidence is perfectly uniform with no semantic divergence: Spanish 'Satanás' throughout, Hindi 'शैतान' / 'शैतान की' / 'शैतान का' (Satan / Satan's), Arabic 'الشَّيْطانُ' / 'الشَّيْطانِ' (the Satan, using the definite article al- with case endings), Korean '사탄이' / '사탄아' / '사탄의' (Satan + subject/vocative/possessive markers), Swahili 'Shetani' / 'wa Shetani' (Satan / of Satan). The Hebrew-origin name (שָׂטָן, adversary) passed through Greek Σατανᾶς into all target languages as a proper noun.
